title: Rust breath and smoke stay a small part of the first-person frame
note: Bright puff pixels cover at most a tenth of the first-person frame during breath or muzzle smoke, else it is a blob.
intent: What matters about breath or gun smoke is how much of the frame it whitens. Draw it with the engine's particles (frame.particles, a pure function of the tick: docs/api/particles.md) started half a metre or more in front of the camera, never at the near plane: five to ten small, low-opacity puffs per breath that drift away from the camera rather than across it. If the frame still washes out, move the emitter forward; do not lower the opacity until it disappears. Capture the default first-person camera during the effect (a demo that breathes or fires) and read the frame before tuning anything else.

check.note: Captured during the breath or smoke effect from the first-person default camera: bright puff pixels cover at most ~10% of the frame.

port: The effects facet owns the emitters and a demo that shows the effect; the default camera is the player's.

evidence.note: Emitters drawn as a pure function of the tick.
The three.js recipe fps.breath-not-a-blob, ported to the genex facade (bodycam B4).
